svg.title: Preventive maintenance, repairs and alterations: who may do what
svg.desc: Preventive maintenance is simple or minor preservation and replacement of small standard parts, limited to the items in 14 CFR part 43 appendix A. Certificated pilots, excluding student, sport and recreational pilots, may do it on aircraft they own or operate, and must make a maintenance record entry with a description, date and pilot name, signature, certificate number and type. Major repairs and alterations are approved on FAA Form 337 by a repair station, an A&P with IA or an FAA representative; minor ones by an A&P or repair station with a maintenance record entry.
svg.text: Preventive maintenance, repairs and alterations: who may do what
Maintenance is the preservation, inspection, overhaul and repair of an aircraft, including the
replacement of parts.
Preventive maintenance
Simple or minor preservation operations and
replacement of small standard parts, not
involving complex assembly operations
Allowed items are listed and limited to 14 CFR
part 43, appendix A(c)
Examples from part 43: landing gear tires and
shock cords, and servicing shock struts with oil
or air; replacing safety wiring and cotter keys;
replenishing hydraulic fluid; replacing or
cleaning spark plugs; cleaning or replacing fuel
and oil strainers or filter elements; servicing
batteries; replacing bulbs, reflectors and lenses
of position and landing lights
Who may do it
Certificated pilots, excluding student pilots,
sport pilots and recreational pilots, on any
aircraft they own or operate, if it is not used
in air carrier service and does not qualify under
14 CFR parts 121, 129 or 135
A sport pilot may do it on an aircraft the pilot
owns or operates that has a special airworthiness
certificate in the LSA category
Every pilot who does it must make an entry in the
aircraft maintenance record
The maintenance entry has three parts
Description of the work, e.g.
"changed oil (Shell Aero-50)
at 2,345 hours"
Date the work was completed
Pilot's name, signature,
certificate number and type of
certificate
Repairs and alterations are classified as major or minor (part 43, appendix A describes the major ones)
Major repair or alteration
Approved for return to service on FAA Form 337,
Major Repair and Alteration
Approved by an appropriately rated certificated
repair station, an A&P mechanic holding an IA, or
a representative of the Administrator
Minor repair or alteration
May be approved for return to service with a
proper entry in the maintenance records
Approved by an FAA-certificated A&P mechanic or
an appropriately certificated repair station
For modifications of experimental aircraft, refer to the operating limitations issued to that aircraft
Repairs or modifications and added equipment may change the weight and balance, so records must be
updated
